The PhD will last from 2027-2031 (4 years). Project background How can housing support a shift towards more sustainable ways of living? The overall research project investigates the potential of housing cooperatives in Switzerland as agents of socio-ecological transition. Moving beyond their established role in providing affordable housing, the project examines how housing cooperatives develop innovative social, spatial, and ecological practices across diverse territorial contexts. original_text: Community-Powered Cities - Unlocking local renewable energy in Greater Newcastle to deliver a more affordable, resilient and sustainable future PhD Scholarship The research will investigate the economic, energy and community benefits and pathways for a city to improve its use of local renewable energy, in a way that is accessible and beneficial to the community, using the Newcastle region as a case study. The study will look at how a city can unlock the potential of distributed energy resources within cities and industrial centres through coordinated deployment of rooftop solar, community energy, battery storage, demand flexibility, electrification, V2G and smart energy management systems. Newcastle presents a unique opportunity to demonstrate the model. As Australia's largest regional city, Newcastle is undertaking a significant transition from a traditional energy economy, while retaining major industrial loads, strong renewable energy opportunities, emerging clean energy industries and ambitious climate goals. While the research will be shaped by early investigations, it may include: - Review national and international examples of urban energy zones and distributed energy precincts - Assess Newcastle's renewable energy resources, energy demand profile, grid constraints and opportunities. - Quantify economic, emissions reduction, resilience and social benefits of a Newcastle UREZ. - Engage government, network opera … mplementation roadmap. - Policy recommendations for state and local government - Peer-reviewed journal publications. - Industry reports and conference presentations. title: Doctoral student (Licentiate) in evaluation and policy for nature-based solutions
why_it_matches: Combines sustainability policy analysis with systemic evaluation of nature‑based solutions, matching the candidate’s interest in sustainable consumption systems and political economy.
original_text: Doctoral student (Licentiate) in evaluation and policy for nature-based solutions KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Architecture and Built Environment Project description Third-cycle subject: Sustainability studies We are seeking applicants with an interest in wetland restoration as a nature-based solution for sustainable water supply under changing climate conditions. The will combine methods such as policy analysis, value mapping, socio-economic analysis, and qualitative research methods. The overall aim is to develop policy and valuation frameworks that link wetland indicators to societal benefits and costs, as well as to practical policy instruments and financing mechanisms. The successful applicant will primarily contribute to: (1) developing policy-relevant indicators for the water-related benefits of restored wetlands and exploring how these can be translated into information relevant for valuation, decision-making, and policy development; and (2) analyzing and mapping the values generated by wetland restoration for different stakeholders and society as a whole, including benefits, costs, and risks, as well as how these are distributed among different actors. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with researchers and societal stakeholders in two interdisciplinary research projects.
